title: A food Calorie is the heat that raises a kilogram of water by one degree
summary: OpenStax distinguishes the nutritional Calorie, which heats one kilogram of water by one degree Celsius, from the small calorie.
body: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology says the energy needed or eaten per day is measured in calories. The nutritional Calorie, written with a capital C, is the amount of heat it takes to raise 1 kilogram of water by 1 degree Celsius. The calorie used in the physical sciences, a small c, raises 1 gram of water by 1 degree Celsius. When people say calorie about food, the textbook says they mean the nutritional Calorie. Carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins in food are used for energy to power activity at the molecular, cellular, and organ level. This is the 25 April 2013 textbook's definition, paraphrased, not a personal energy prescription.
